title: Internal Hom of constant modules with finitely presented source
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, and let $P,Q$ be $\Lambda$-modules. Assume $P$ is finitely presented, meaning that there are finite integers $a,b\geq0$ and an exact sequence $\Lambda^a\to\Lambda^b\to P\to0$. Use the constant module sheaves $\underline P,\underline Q,\underline\Lambda$ of [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor], and the ordinary sheaf Hom of [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. The canonical $\underline\Lambda$-linear map
$$
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(P,Q)}\longrightarrow
\mathcal Hom_{\underline\Lambda}(\underline P,\underline Q)
$$
sending a locally represented constant linear map $f:P\to Q$ to the corresponding map of constant module sheaves is an isomorphism. The map is natural in $P,Q$ and uses the same constant linear map after restriction to any localized site $\mathcal C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No finite generation of $Q$, finiteness of $\Lambda$, or hypothesis on points of $\mathcal C$ is imposed.

proof.text: For F=constantModuleHomFunctor, construct the linear constant-section unit after transport along constantModuleHomRingIso. Its underlying additive map is toSheafify, hence locally bijective. For any M,N and U send a linear map f to restrictOver(F(f)) on U. To check additivity and compatibility with constant scalars, use naturality of toSheafify and the unit scalar equation; the equality of local maps follows by representing each input section locally by a constant and applying separatedness. This gives a morphism from the constant Hom module presheaf to the internal Hom with scalars restricted to the constant ring.

Extend this linear map along the locally bijective constant-module unit using Mathlib PresheafOfModules.homEquivOfIsLocallyBijective. Then apply restrictHomEquivOfIsLocallySurjective for the constant-ring unit to obtain a map linear over the entire constant ring sheaf. The two hom equivalences are induced by precomposition/restriction, so their inverse equations give exactly the required constant-section formula.

For a finitely generated M, equality of two constant local maps implies that their values on each of finitely many generators have equal unit images. Intersect the corresponding covering equalizer sieves. On every arrow in the intersection the constant linear maps agree on the generators and thus agree. For finitely presented M and a local map x over U, compose the unit of M with x at the identity of U to get a linear map from M to sections of F(N). Apply [lem-sf-finite-presentation-local-linear-lift] to the locally bijective linear unit of N. Each resulting lift g:M→N induces the restriction of x: first check constants using naturality on the slice, then all sections by local constant representatives and separatedness. Thus the same additive constant-Hom comparison is locally bijective.

The composite of the comparison with the constant-Hom unit is the locally bijective map of the preceding step. Cancel that locally bijective unit to show the comparison is locally injective and locally surjective. Apply the Mathlib locally-bijective isomorphism criterion to its underlying additive sheaf morphism, and reflect isomorphisms through SheafOfModules.toSheaf. This proves IsIso for P,Q when P is finitely presented.

For naturality precompose both composites with the constant-Hom sheafification unit. By its universal property it suffices to compare constant f. The unit formula and functoriality identify both sides with F(a≫f≫b) restricted to the slice; homObjMap is precisely pre- and post-composition. For the stated localization equation, specialize the constant-section formula to V.left and evaluate the resulting local map at the identity of V.left. The definitions of over and restrictOver give exactly the requested restricted map.

lean.statement: theorem siteConstantModule_hom (P Q : ModuleCat.{max u v} Λ) [Module.FinitePresentation Λ P] : ∃ comparison : ∀ M N : ModuleCat.{max u v} Λ, (constantModuleHomFunctor J Λ).obj (ModuleCat.of Λ (M →ₗ[Λ] N)) ⟶ SheafOfModules.homObj (R := (constantSheaf J CommRingCat.{max u v}).obj (CommRingCat.of Λ)) ((constantModuleHomFunctor J Λ).obj M) ((constantModuleHomFunctor J Λ).obj N), (∀ (M N : ModuleCat.{max u v} Λ) (U : Cᵒᵖ) (f : M →ₗ[Λ] N), (comparison M N).val.app U ((constantModuleHomUnit J Λ (ModuleCat.of Λ (M →ₗ[Λ] N))).app U f) = (PresheafOfModules.restrictOver ((constantSheaf J CommRingCat.{max u v}).obj (CommRingCat.of Λ)).obj U.unop).map (((constantModuleHomFunctor J Λ).map (ModuleCat.ofHom f)).val)) ∧ IsIso (comparison P Q) ∧ (∀ (M M' N N' : ModuleCat.{max u v} Λ) (a : M' ⟶ M) (b : N ⟶ N'), (constantModuleHomFunctor J Λ).map (ModuleCat.ofHom ((LinearMap.llcomp Λ M' N N' b.hom).comp (LinearMap.lcomp Λ N a.hom))) ≫ comparison M' N' = comparison M N ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := (constantSheaf J CommRingCat.{max u v}).obj (CommRingCat.of Λ)) ((constantModuleHomFunctor J Λ).map a) ((constantModuleHomFunctor J Λ).map b)) ∧ (∀ (U : C) (V : Over U) (f : P →ₗ[Λ] Q), (((comparison P Q).over U).val.app (op V) ((constantModuleHomUnit J Λ (ModuleCat.of Λ (P →ₗ[Λ] Q))).app (op V.left) f)).app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 V.left))) = (((constantModuleHomFunctor J Λ).map (ModuleCat.ofHom f)).over U).val.app (op V))
